`public/models/helmet.glb` now uses about 7 MiB of GPU memory, down from 107 MiB. The file is 3.30 MB, down from 3.77 MB.

- **Fidelity:** the worst-case SSIM against the original is 0.94, above the 0.9 limit the tool recommends for no visible quality loss. The side-by-side preview looks identical to me.
- **Method:** I ran `node-assets tune --for gpu` and applied the best result. Textures are KTX2 (ETC1S for color, UASTC for data) at up to 1024px, and geometry is quantized. The `--check` run passed.
- **Decoder:** the output needs the KTX2 transcoder. Your Babylon.js scene loads it automatically, as you said.
- **Source untouched:** `assets/helmet.glb` is unchanged. The recipe is saved at `recipes/helmet.gpu.recipe.json`, with a preview image and the full candidate table alongside it, in case you want to rerun it on other models.
bash_cmds: node-assets --help 2>&1 | head -80; echo ---; ls -la assets public/models 2>&1; echo ---; pwd; ls -la
node-assets inspect assets/helmet.glb --view 1024 2>&1 | head -150; echo ---; node-assets tune --help 2>&1 | head -80
mkdir -p recipes && node-assets tune assets/helmet.glb --for gpu -o recipes/ 2>&1 | tail -80
node-assets run --help 2>&1 | head -40; echo ---; cat recipes/helmet.gpu.recipe.json; echo; cmp assets/helmet.glb public/models/helmet.glb && echo "public copy identical to source"

node-assets run recipes/helmet.gpu.recipe.json assets/helmet.glb -o public/models/helmet.glb --check --force 2>&1 | tail -40; echo ---; node-assets inspect public/models/helmet.glb --against assets/helmet.glb --view 1024 2>&1 | head -80; echo ---; ls -la public/models/helmet.glb assets/helmet.glb
